newsitem.title: CHINA: Rents to take 15 percent of salaries in China.
newsitem.headline: Rents to take 15 percent of salaries in China.

text.p: Chinese state employees will see their rent payments increased to 15 percent of their salaries by the year 2000 from a current 3.64 percent, a government official said on Monday.

"If we do not raise home rents, reform of the housing system may face a series of problems," an official of the Leading Group for the Reform of the Housing System of the State Council said in a telephone interview.

In 1996, rents accounted for only 3.64 percent of the average salary of state employees, including civil servants and workers in state enterprises, in 35 major cities, while in towns the average was just one percent, the official said.

However, a one percent increase in rents pushed up consumer price inflation by 0.4 percent making it difficult to strike a balance between appropriately raising rents while curbing inflation, the official said.
"In principle, rents will be raised to 15 percent (of salaries) by 2000, but personally I don't think it can reach that high," he said by telephone.
Currently, the government subsidises housing with most Chinese paying almost negligible rents for extremely basic homes, often without bathrooms or hot running water.
China has tried in recent years to raise rents as part of a drive to create a real housing market in China, but has been hampered by fears of worker unrest as well as soaring inflation.

Retail price inflation hit a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994 before falling back to 14.8 percent in 1995, and 6.1 percent last year. Inflation this year is forecast to be between three and four percent.
